title: Assurance walkthrough: RBACv2, audit-log exports, and evidence matrix
content:
Executive summary:

Purpose: A concise, auditor-facing walkthrough tying RBACv2 controls, the standardized audit-log schema, and our SIEM export pipeline to the specific SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control objectives. This is meant for a dry-run with auditors and for the engineering owners to validate evidence automation outputs before the formal attestation window.

Scope: RBACv2 enforcement surface (console, API, private deployments control plane), audit log capture and retention, SIEM export pipelines (ingest transforms), and the evidence automation playbook used to assemble auditor bundles. Not in scope: third-party vendor controls and application-layer business logic telemetry.

Audience: Security/compliance engineers, SREs responsible for log exports, auditors, and product owners for Private and Dedicated offerings.

Structure of this doc: mapping summary, audit-log schema highlights, SIEM export checklist, evidence automation plan, prioritized gap analysis, and curated auditor Q&A with required extracts.

1) Mapping summary (control intent -> artifact):
- Control: Logical access reviews (ISO A.9 / SOC2 CC6) -> Artifacts: RBACv2 role definitions, group membership snapshots, access-review ticket history, policy change events in audit logs.
- Control: Least privilege and role separation (ISO A.9.2 / SOC2 CC6.1) -> Artifacts: role-to-permission matrix, recent permission delta events, approval workflow records.
- Control: Logging of privileged actions and detection (ISO A.12 / SOC2 CC7) -> Artifacts: normalized audit-log exports, SIEM detection rule hits, alert runbooks.
- Control: Evidence retention and integrity (ISO A.8 / SOC2 CC3) -> Artifacts: S3 archive manifests, checksum records, retention-policy config, KMS-wrapped snapshots.

Each mapping above corresponds to specific log event types (see audit-log schema section) and to pull queries we will provide for the auditor runbook.

2) Audit-log schema highlights (engineer-friendly brief):
We standardized the audit-log schema to make auditor extracts repeatable across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Important fields (present on every event):
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- event_id: stable UUID v4
- user_id: internal employee id or service principal id (hashed for PII exports)
- user_email: email (redaction flag available)
- actor_type: user | service | system
- action: canonical action verb (e.g., role.assign, role.remove, policy.update, token.issue, token.revoke, login.failed)
- resource_type: route | console | model | deployment | key
- resource_id: canonical id (tenant:model:deployment)
- outcome: success | failure | throttled
- ip_address: client ip (redacted in export if requested)
- request_context: path and HTTP method (truncated)
- kv_before / kv_after: compact delta of object state (limited length; archived full snapshot in artifact store)
- trace_id: correlation id for multi-hop traces
- retention_tier: hot | warm | archive

Field notes: kv_before/kv_after are summary strings (not full JSON) in the live stream to avoid PII and size bloat; full snapshots are retained in the artifact store and referenced by snapshot_id. For auditor bundles we include snapshot_id references and accompanying ETags.

3) SIEM export pipeline specifics:
- Export frequency: rolling 24h batch + near-real-time stream for critical events (privileged changes, token revocations).
- Transformations applied: timestamp canonicalization, event-type normalization, redact-if-PII, enrich-with-asset-tags (env, region, customer_tier).
- Packaging for auditors: daily export bundle includes manifest.csv (md5, object_key, snapshot_id, retention_tier), event-tail.csv (canonical events), and evidence-metadata.json (human readable mapping). For privacy-sensitive customers we produce a redacted bundle variant.
- Retention: hot (30d) -> warm (180d) -> archive (7 years) depending on control needs; retention_tier is present on each event.

4) Evidence automation playbook (practical steps to build auditor bundle):
- Step A: Identify control set and timeframe (e.g., access reviews for Q4 2025).
- Step B: Run queries: (1) role_definitions snapshot, (2) membership-deltas between T0 and T1, (3) privilege-change events filtered by action.role.*, (4) snapshot artifact IDs for each changed object.
- Step C: Resolve full snapshots: call artifact-store list with snapshot_ids to export full JSON and ETag.
- Step D: Build manifest.csv: columns = artifact_key, snapshot_id, etag, size_bytes, md5, control_mapping_tag.
- Step E: Generate human summary: for each artifact include a 2–3 sentence explanation of why it maps to the control (this dramatically speeds auditor reviews).
- Step F: Package and notarize: sign manifest with KMS key-id and include kms_signing_meta.txt.

Runbook commands (examples):
- Query role snapshots: SELECT * FROM role_snapshots WHERE snapshot_time BETWEEN '2025-10-01' AND '2025-12-31';
- Fetch audit events: airflow trigger dag=siem_export --start=2025-10-01 --end=2025-12-31 --include=action.role.assign,action.role.remove;
- Resolve snapshots: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARTIFACT_TOKEN" https://artifact-store.company/snapshots/{snapshot_id} > snapshot-{snapshot_id}.json

5) Prioritized gap analysis (concise remediation backlog):
- Gap 1 (P0): Missing automated assignment of snapshot ETags into manifest for some legacy snapshots. Impact: auditor cannot verify integrity without manual steps. Remediation: add lambda to compute ETags at snapshot creation and backfill for existing snapshots (owner: infra, ETA: 3 sprints).
- Gap 2 (P1): Some RBAC change events logged with user_email null when an SSO session timed out before the change action was committed. Impact: occasional incomplete identity trail. Remediation: implement actor_fallback lookup using session-token metadata and backfill recent 90d via session logs (owner: auth, ETA: 2 sprints).
- Gap 3 (P2): Retention metadata occasionally set to default instead of explicit tier during bulk imports. Impact: possible premature archival. Remediation: add validation in import pipeline and alert on implicit-tier writes (owner: data-platform, ETA: 1 sprint).

6) Auditor Q&A (curated and mapped to exact evidence extracts):
Q: "How do you prove role changes were authorized?"
A: Provide the role-change event stream (2025-10-01..2025-12-31), the associated approval workflow ticket IDs (in the kv_before/kv_after or request_context), and the snapshot JSON for role-definitions both before and after the change. Attach manifest entries: control_mapping_tag=access-review. See manifest row: artifact_key=role-snapshot-2025-11-02.json.

Q: "Where do you store immutable copies of audit logs and how can I validate integrity?"
A: Immutable copies are S3 objects in the archive bucket with server-side encryption and object-versioning enabled. Provide manifest.csv with md5 and ETag; auditors can validate by downloading and comparing with manifest md5. KMS signing metadata is included to validate origin.

Q: "Can you show examples of failed privileged actions and your alerting response?"
A: Export event set with outcome=failure and action in privileged set, plus SIEM alert id and response runbook excerpt (we include a redacted runbook and the alert timeline).

Q: "How do you ensure the same schema across dedicated/private deployments?"
A: We publish a schema contract (Confluence page CONFLUENCE-SEC-LOGSCHEMA-1) and a nightly conformance job that runs schema checks and raises JIRA tickets when deviations occur. Include the last 30-day conformance report.

7) Packaging and handoff checklist for auditor dry-run (quick):
- [ ] Confirm timeframe and control list with auditor.
- [ ] Run evidence automation and produce manifest.csv.
- [ ] Verify checksums and sign manifest.
- [ ] Produce redacted and full bundles where required.
- [ ] Upload to secure transfer location and provide one-time-download link + expiration.
- [ ] Walk auditor through a 30-minute bundle review session.

8) Example extracts (text examples to reduce back-and-forth):
- Example event line (CSV friendly):
2025-11-02T14:23:12Z,0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e,UID-1324,a.patel@example.com,user,role.assign,role,role:infra-admin,success,34.23.11.2,/api/v1/roles/assign,kbref:role-snap-2025-11-02,trace-1,hot

- Example manifest line:
role-snapshot-2025-11-02.json,role-snap-2025-11-02,etag-abc123,31245,9b2d4f3a,access-review

9) Ownership and escalation matrix: who to call when an auditor asks for follow-ups:
- Audit evidence runner / primary: Aisha Patel (security-compliance) — aisha.patel@redwood.com
- SIEM export engineer: Marco Chen (observability) — marco.chen@redwood.com
- Artifact store owner: Elena Gomez (infra) — elena.gomez@redwood.com
- Auth owner (RBACv2): Samir Rao (platform-engineering) — samir.rao@redwood.com

10) Appendix: lightweight checklist for a dry-run walkthrough session (30–45 minutes)
- 0–5m: Introductions and scope confirmation.
- 5–15m: Show end-to-end map: control -> event type -> snapshot -> manifest row.
- 15–25m: Demonstrate export: run the query and show artifact download + checksum verification.
- 25–35m: Walk through conformance report and open gaps.
- 35–45m: Agree on follow-ups and timeline.

Notes and constraints: this doc intentionally omits customer-specific PII. When preparing bundles for a customer-backed audit, follow the redaction checklist in CONFLUENCE-SEC-REDACT-2 and coordinate with legal for any contractual constraints.

Appendix references (tickets & pages): CONFLUENCE-SEC-LOGSCHEMA-1, JIRA-SEC-4832 (ETag backfill), CONFLUENCE-SEC-REDACT-2.

End of document.
